subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What permanent API shape should OpenClaw expose for Telegram custom emoji entities: raw Telegram `entities`/`caption_entities`, a portable Markdown/rich-text IR span, or Telegram-only channel data?
rationale: Current main already supports `<tg-emoji>` HTML passthrough, but the reported production gap is the message-tool entity round trip; that changes shared tool/plugin API shape and needs maintainer product judgment before implementation.

options.title: Design Shared Rich-Text Entity API
options.body: Add a typed representation that can carry custom emoji IDs through the shared message tool and let Telegram map it to Bot API entities or rich HTML.

options.title: Expose Telegram-Only Entities
options.body: Add a narrow Telegram-owned `channelData.telegram.entities` or `caption_entities` path with validation and tests, accepting that it is not portable across channels.

options.title: Document HTML-Only Support
options.body: Keep current `<tg-emoji>` HTML/rich-text support as the supported path and close narrower entity-array requests as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Rich-Text Entity API
recommendation.body: Add a typed representation that can carry custom emoji IDs through the shared message tool and let Telegram map it to Bot API entities or rich HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: Focused blame, prior issue review, and recent message-tool/Telegram history point to steipete as the strongest API-shape reviewer for this area.
